items.title: GAO finds the acting director of the Institute of Education Sciences is serving unlawfully
items.summary: GAO determined that Matthew Soldner’s service as acting director of the Institute of Education Sciences has violated the Federal Vacancies Reform Act since November 19, 2025. The permissible acting-service period expired after an earlier nomination was returned, but the Education Department continued to identify him as acting director. GAO notes that, once the statutory period ends, the office must remain vacant and only the agency head may perform its nondelegable functions.

items.title: FTC considers duties for platforms that amplify government and business impersonation scams
items.summary: The FTC opened—not completed—an advance rulemaking inquiry on whether search engines, social platforms, and other digital marketplaces should face specific duties when their systems further government or business impersonation scams. The current rule reaches impersonators but not necessarily platforms that optimize fraudulent ads. The commission asks whether a new rule should make platforms internalize those costs; comments are due November 30. The notice is a request for evidence, not a final prohibition.

items.title: DHS raises parole, ESTA, and EVUS fees under statutory inflation formulas
items.summary: DHS announced statutory inflation adjustments effective October 16: the parole fee rises from $1,020 to $1,050, ESTA from $40.27 to $40.62, and EVUS enrollment from $30.75 to $31.75; the land-border I-94 application fee remains $30 after rounding. The notice calculates a 3.36% CPI-U increase but applies different statutory rounding rules. The parole charge attaches when parole is actually granted, subject to ten case-by-case exceptions, regardless of application date.

items.title: State Department replaces the blanket Syria defense-trade denial policy with case-by-case licensing
items.summary: A State Department final rule removes Syria from ITAR’s list of countries subject to a comprehensive policy of denial for defense-export and import licenses. It does not create general approval: applications will instead receive case-by-case review. The department says the relevant statutory prerequisites were satisfied, including rescission or waiver of separate terrorism, chemical-weapons, Syria-accountability, and child-soldier restrictions. Effective immediately on October 1, the change materially reopens a licensing channel without guaranteeing any license.

items.title: GAO estimates that 86% of high-risk U.S. properties lack federal flood insurance
items.summary: GAO estimates that 86% of high-risk U.S. properties lacked National Flood Insurance Program coverage in April 2026, with about 13 million high-risk properties outside FEMA special flood hazard areas. Coverage is far more common where federally backed mortgages trigger a purchase requirement: 43% inside those areas versus 2% outside. GAO urges Congress to incorporate rainfall risk, publish property-level risk, require lenders to quote insurance, and raise NFIP limits; these are recommendations, not enacted changes.

items.title: SEC approves clearer stress tests and guaranty-fund rules for CME Securities Clearing
items.summary: SEC approved changes to CME Securities Clearing’s stress-testing and guaranty-fund documentation. The clearinghouse sizes its fund to cover losses above initial margin from the two member families producing the largest theoretical exposure, then allocates contributions mainly by relative exposure and partly by gross notional. The revisions describe historical and hypothetical scenarios, interest-rate shocks, principal-component analysis, and the rationale for the “cover two” standard. The order approves transparency and alignment changes rather than a new fund level.

items.title: Commerce preliminarily assigns roughly 47%–51% dumping margins to Chinese truck-bed covers
items.summary: Commerce preliminarily found that truck-bed covers from China were sold in the United States below fair value during July–December 2025. Calculated dumping margins were 51.35% for Hangzhou Golden Sun, 46.95% for Wenzhou Tianmao/Chaoming, and 49.56% for named separate-rate combinations; cash-deposit rates are slightly lower after subsidy offsets. The China-wide entity is subject to adverse-inference methodology. These are preliminary administrative findings, open to briefing before a final determination.

items.title: Commerce preliminarily finds subsidies for Chinese air-compressor producers
items.summary: Commerce preliminarily found countervailable subsidies for Chinese stationary and portable air-compressor producers. It calculated 3.84% for FNA (Zhejiang) and all other eligible producers, while assigning 112.29% to several firms on adverse facts available after concluding respondents had not cooperated fully. Customs will suspend liquidation of covered entries. The final subsidy determination is aligned with the companion antidumping case and is currently due by February 10, 2027; the rates remain preliminary.

items.title: GAO finds federal SNAP outreach to food-insecure veterans is outdated
items.summary: GAO reports that a cited RAND study estimated an average 1.4 million veterans experienced food insecurity annually from 2015 through 2020, while eligible veterans participate in SNAP less often than nonveterans. Although 39 of 47 states with federally approved outreach plans targeted veterans in fiscal 2026, USDA has not produced tailored, current veteran outreach materials in five years. GAO recommends updated materials and clearer myth-correction tools for trusted intermediaries.

items.title: CBO estimates a foreign-visitor threat-analysis bill would cost $10 million over five years
items.summary: CBO estimates H.R. 7427 would cost $10 million over 2027–2031, subject to appropriation: $5 million for the equivalent of three DHS employees to analyze threats from certain foreign visitors to state and local officials and facilities, and $5 million for a threat-information-sharing system. It projects no direct-spending or revenue effect and no intergovernmental or private-sector mandate. The estimate describes the House committee version; it does not predict enactment or program effectiveness.

items.title: CBO prices a Brazilian Amazon security and conservation bill at $25 million
items.summary: CBO estimates the Senate committee version of S. 2578 would add $25 million in appropriated spending over 2027–2031 and have insignificant net effects on direct spending. The bill would authorize U.S. technical assistance to disrupt criminal networks in the Brazilian Amazon, promote economic development and environmental protection, and direct Treasury advocacy at international financial institutions. The estimate prices specified federal activity; it does not quantify avoided deforestation, enforcement results, or broader economic effects.

items.title: FTA proposes immediate new guidance for transit capital grants, including projects already in the pipeline
items.summary: FTA proposes a comprehensive rewrite of guidance for Capital Investment Grants used by New Starts, Small Starts, and Core Capacity transit projects. The agency says it would simplify duplicated category-by-category material, change process and evaluation requirements, and strengthen sponsor accountability. Once final, the guidance would apply immediately to projects already in the pipeline—there is no grandfathering. Twenty-two respondents informed the proposal; comments are due November 16, so the revisions are not yet binding.

items.title: GAO exposes biosecurity gaps in federal sales of surplus laboratory equipment
items.summary: GAO found HHS and USDA sold or transferred 1,316 pieces of surplus laboratory equipment in fiscal 2022–2025 without a comprehensive biosecurity-risk process. Nine sold items were on the Commerce Control List, yet agencies did not flag them to GSA as required. Using fictitious identities, investigators also acquired four devices experts said could pose biosecurity risks. GAO recommends reporting controls and regular risk assessments; the demonstration shows procurement vulnerability, not evidence that buyers misused equipment.

items.title: FDA cannot fully measure the timeliness of scientific reviews for tobacco products
items.summary: GAO found FDA reduced a tobacco-product authorization backlog that began with more than 25 million applications, but nearly 132,000 applications remained incomplete at the end of 2025. Reviews completed from 2018–2025 averaged 507 days. FDA had phase-specific targets, yet its system could not track performance during the final scientific-review phase, preventing a complete timeliness assessment. GAO recommends collecting those data; the report evaluates review management and does not determine whether pending products are safe or legally marketable.

items.title: Preprint links minimal hypersurface volume to curvature and boundary geometry
items.summary: Sanghun Lee’s eight-page preprint proves a volume estimate for stable, volume-minimizing free-boundary hypersurfaces in high-dimensional Riemannian manifolds. The bound links hypersurface volume to the ambient manifold’s scalar curvature and the second fundamental form of its boundary, with rigidity results for equality cases. The work is a mathematical theorem, not an empirical estimate, but it is a first-version arXiv preprint submitted October 1 and has not been presented here as peer reviewed.
